New from Yakima Bait is the Trout Twitcher Jig, a lure that combines lifelike movements of natural and artificial furs and feathers designed to produce more and bigger trout. The Trout Twitcher features several components along with years of testing aimed at triggering aggressive response from predatory fish.
p

Wherever trout are found, the Trout Twitcher gives anglers a versatile presentation that mimics live bait with a series of swift, short hops and twitches. Twitched, jigged, retrieved or stripped like a streamer, it gives off a copycat wounded baitfish movement that larger trout try to remove from the food chain. “Breathing” natural materials like rabbit fur strip and palmered hackle work together to impart life-like movement that does not cease, even when held still. It continues as the jig falls, rises, drifts with current or pauses, suggesting a dying or wounded sculpin, crayfish or similarly sized baitfish.
p

Each jig is professionally tied on round, easily swum chip-proof painted heads paired with strong 1/0 sized 2x hooks that hold their sharpness through bottom contact with rocks and gravel, plus multiple hookups. The Trout Twitcher moves realistically when hopped or twitched with current in rivers and streams or in still water lakes and reservoirs.
p

Available in two sizes, 1/8 ounce and 1/4 ounce. The 1/8-ounce size is made for shallower and smaller rivers, streams and shorter casts in the shallow sections of lakes. The 1/4-ounce allows for longer casts and quicker sinking, ideal for targeting deeper water. Each individually packaged Trout Twitcher comes with a clear vinyl protector/safety tube fixed to the tine of the hook.
p

The new Trout Twitchers will be available in 10 colors, primarily layered and blended in natural baitfish tones including Black, Black/Red, Brown/Red, Olive/Brown, Olive/Red, Red/Grey, plus attraction colors of Red/White, bright Pink, White and Brown/Yellow. The range of colors makes it simple to match water clarity, lighting conditions and fish preference.
p
The Trout Twitchers are also effective for bass anglers — smallmouth primarily, but all species of bass and walleye eagerly strike jigs, especially those with natural toned and blended shades.
p

A standout feature of the Yakima Bait Trout Twitcher is the adjustable tail. Each tail is tied with a 2-inch-long rabbit strip; with sharp scissors, anglers may cut only the rabbit skin (not the fur) to snip off any length of tail to match the whims of trout and copy their preferred food size, without sacrificing the imparted action of the tail.
p

The new Trout Twitchers are primarily a light-tackle presentation. Ideal rod lengths for rivers and lakes are 7 foot, 7-1/2 foot (most popular) and 8 foot, with line ratings from 2 to 6 pound and 4 to 8 up to 4 to 10 pound test. Spinning reels should be of the 1000 series, spooled with thin, brightly colored braid such as 10, 12 or 15-pound test. A bright line can be followed easily near obstructions. A 6- to 7-foot “top shot” section of either 6-, 8- or 10-pound natural toned monofilament or clear fluorocarbon should be tied to the bright braid. A suggested 1-inch diameter loop knot will open up the action of the jig, allowing it to tilt freely rather than pulling directly on the jig head and restricting its vertical movement.
p

When legal, the recommended way to apply scent is with water-soluble Yakima Bait Rooster Tail spray scents, with the Trophy Trout flavor highly recommended. The water-soluble scent will not matte down the rabbit fur/hackle and allows it to work with maximum action while still releasing a scent trail. Anglers can also place a single white Berkley Gulp Maggot on the hook bend for a durable scent trail.
p
